description: Per-country localization profiles: factual, citable locale data the ingestion engine merges into each country's overlay.json. This is the SAFE localization layer — official/patient-facing languages, national formulary linkage (by registry source id), and whether national guidelines derive from WHO. It deliberately contains NO clinical recommendations; dosing/protocol overlays are authored separately and gated on clinical sign-off. ISO 639-1 language codes; nationalFormularySource references content/sources/registry.json ids.

UG.name: Uganda
UG.notes: Uganda Clinical Guidelines (UCG) and EMHSLU; English is the health-system working language, Swahili is co-official.

TZ.name: Tanzania
TZ.notes: Standard Treatment Guidelines + NEMLIT; Swahili is the primary national language, English used in clinical practice.

RW.name: Rwanda
RW.notes: English is the medium of health-professional training; Kinyarwanda for patient-facing content. French and Swahili also official.

ET.name: Ethiopia
ET.notes: Amharic is the federal working language; English is used in higher/medical education. Oromo is a major additional language.

NG.name: Nigeria
NG.notes: English is the official and clinical language; Hausa, Yoruba and Igbo are major languages for later patient-facing localization.

GH.name: Ghana
GH.notes: English is the official and clinical language; Akan/Twi is the most widely spoken local language.

ZA.name: South Africa
ZA.notes: English is the clinical lingua franca; South Africa has 12 official languages. STGs + EDL by PHC/hospital level.

ZM.name: Zambia
ZM.notes: English is the official and clinical language; Bemba and Nyanja are major local languages.

MW.name: Malawi
MW.notes: English is the official language; Chichewa (ny) is the most widely spoken and used for patient-facing content.
